Ben / Kim —

Quick technical note from my initial look through acme_run-20270712.json:
- The harness shows batch_size=1 but the run tool sets a synthetic batching window of 50ms (client-side). That can mask per-request TTFT by aggregating micro-batches.
- Tokenization mismatch: your logs indicate a SentencePiece model deriving 140 tokens vs our tokenization baseline at 128 for the same prompt (20% increase in token work).
- Runtime path: we sometimes observe a CPU fallback when quant kernels aren't available for the specific CUDA/driver combo; this shows up as elevated tail latency under concurrency.
- KV cache warmup: your harness appears to skip prefix warmup which increases first-request TTFT for long contexts.

What I'll do:
- Try an exact reproduction on a g4dn.xlarge with the same driver/kernel combo you listed.
- Run two variants: 1) customer-harness mode (exact commands you sent) and 2) Redwood-canonical mode (our MAP config).
- Collect kernel traces and nvprof slices for comparison.

I've attached redwood_repro_template.yaml — please run it and return the output. That will speed the triage.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Discrepancy in MAP perf numbers (TTFT / concurrency) — triage summary + MAP timeline update

Team — final sync/update and proposed close plan. Key findings from Redwood reproduction attempt and initial triage:
- Root cause (primary): tooling divergence — your harness hit a runtime codepath that caused quantized kernels to fallback to a CPU-emulation path under the customer CUDA/driver combo. This increased tail latency substantially at concurrency >4.
- Secondary: tokenization differences (your SentencePiece variant produced ~10-12% more tokens for the same prompts), and prefix warmup was not consistently enabled in your run.
- Competitive delta note: VendorX appears to ship a runtime with a different quant-kernel set for T4 devices that avoided the fallback. That accounts for some of the difference you observed in the A/B.

What Redwood will do (committed milestones in the MAP doc):
- By Mon 2027-07-18: full reproducible run artifacts (nvprof slices + kernel call traces) delivered to Acme; root-cause packet documented.
- By Wed 2027-07-20: Redwood will prepare a runtime compatibility patch (if feasible) or a mitigation guide (pin driver/kernel or change invocation flags).
- Joint canary: Thu 2027-07-22 10:00 PT — run canary with Redwood engineer and Acme SRE on a g4dn.xlarge to validate mitigations.

Action items:
- Acme: run redwood_repro_template.yaml and share the output by EOD Mon 2027-07-18 (Samantha volunteered).
- Redwood: Marcus to deliver reproducible artifacts and draft mitigation by Mon 2027-07-18.
- Laura to update MAP-ACME-1372-v2.docx with milestones and sign-offs (linked).

If this plan looks good I will update the MAP timeline in HubSpot and mark "blocker: reproduction" as in-progress.

Thanks for the fast collaboration — this should restore parity for the close.

Best,
